question: Proto-oncogenes promote cell growth and proliferation; when mutated into oncogenes, a single mutant allele (gain-of-function) is sufficient to drive malignant transformation.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Oncogenes act dominantly — a single gain-of-function mutation suffices. Tumour suppressor genes (e.g., TP53, RB1) require biallelic loss (two-hit hypothesis) to lose function.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Proto-oncogenes are dominant — one mutant allele (gain-of-function) is enough to dysregulate growth. This contrasts with tumour suppressor genes, which require both alleles to be inactivated (two-hit hypothesis, Knudson).
